name: ICL7107CPLZ
title: ICL7106, ICL7107, ICL7107S: 3 1/2 digit dual-slope A/D converters with LCD or LED display drive
summary: Single-chip 3 1/2 digit (±1999 count) integrating A/D converters with on-chip clock, reference, seven-segment decoders and display drivers. The ICL7106 drives a liquid crystal display with its own backplane signal and runs from one 9 V battery; the ICL7107 sinks current from a common-anode LED display and runs from ±5 V. Inputs and reference are both truly differential, with 1 pA typical input current, auto-zero to under 10 µV and a guaranteed zero reading for 0 V. The ICL7107S is an ICL7107 graded for last-digit stability. ICL7107CPLZ is the ICL7107 in a 40 lead PDIP, 0 °C to 70 °C.
key_figures: 15 µV p-p typ at 200 mV full scale

circuits.title: ICL7106 test circuit and typical application, LCD display, 200 mV full scale
circuits.description: The circuit the ICL7106 is specified in: a 9 V battery across V+ and V-, a 3 1/2 digit LCD on the segment outputs with its backplane on BP. R1 (24 kΩ) from V+ and the 1 kΩ trimmer R4 form the reference divider above COMMON; the wiper sets REF HI, and REF LO, COMMON and IN LO are one node. R5 (1 MΩ) and C5 (0.02 µF) filter the input. C1 is the reference capacitor, C2 the auto-zero capacitor, R2 the integrating resistor and C3 the integrating capacitor; R3 and C4 set the 48 kHz clock.

circuits.title: ICL7106 digital centigrade thermometer
circuits.description: A diode-connected silicon NPN (MPS3704 or similar) on a cable is the sensor, biased by 22 kΩ from V+ with its emitter on COMMON; its base-collector node drives IN LO. A 100 kΩ zero trimmer with 220 kΩ from V+ drives IN HI from its wiper, and a 100 kΩ scale trimmer with 1 MΩ from V+ sets REF HI. The junction drifts about -2 mV/°C. Calibrate the zero trimmer for 000.0 in ice water, then the scale trimmer for 100.0 in boiling water.

circuits.title: Underrange and overrange signals from the ICL7106 outputs
circuits.description: Four CD4077 exclusive-NOR gates compare segment outputs B3, E3, AB4 and G3 with the backplane, turning each LCD drive back into a logic level. CD4023 (or 74C10) NAND gates combine them into active-low O/RANGE and U/RANGE outputs. V+ is the logic supply and TEST the logic ground.

circuits.title: Underrange and overrange signals from the ICL7107 outputs
circuits.description: An LM339 quad comparator turns segment outputs B3, E3, AB4 and G3 into logic levels against a threshold set by 12 kΩ from +5 V and 33 kΩ to ground; the comparators keep the logic levels valid under heavy display load. CD4023 (or 74C10) NAND gates combine them into active-low O/RANGE and U/RANGE outputs.

circuits.title: AC to DC converter with the ICL7106
circuits.description: A CA3140 with 100 kΩ in series with its non-inverting input and 2.2 MΩ feedback (0.22 µF to the return) drives a two-diode 1N914 rectifier through 5 µF. Each rectified half charges 1 µF across 10 kΩ, and a 470 kΩ / 1 µF filter feeds IN HI. 4.3 kΩ with 100 pF across it (for best bandwidth) joins the rectifier return to IN LO. TEST, tied to IN LO and the AC input return, is the common-mode level for the op amp; 10 µF bypasses it to V+ and to V-. The reference trimmer is set for 100 mV for an AC-to-RMS reading.

parts.note: scale factor adjust, VREF = 100 mV for AC to RMS; pins 1 and 2 the track ends, W the wiper

operation.text: Every conversion has three phases. Auto-zero: the inputs are disconnected and shorted inside to COMMON, CREF charges to the reference, and a loop through buffer, integrator and comparator stores their offsets on CAZ, leaving under 10 µV referred to the input, limited by noise. Signal integrate: the loop opens and the IN HI to IN LO difference is integrated for a fixed 1000 counts; its polarity is latched at the end. Deintegrate: IN LO goes to COMMON and IN HI to the charged CREF, connected with the polarity that ramps the integrator back to zero; the time taken is the reading.

The input takes differential signals anywhere from 1 V above V- to 0.5 V below V+, with 86 dB CMRR typical. The integrator can saturate when a big positive common-mode level meets a negative input close to full scale; reducing the integrator swing below the usual 2 V prevents this at small cost in accuracy. The integrator stays linear to within 0.3 V of either supply. An input with no return to the supply can have IN LO tied to COMMON.

The reference may sit anywhere within the supply. Stray capacitance on the CREF nodes makes CREF gain charge when deintegrating one polarity and lose it on the other under a large common-mode voltage, giving rollover error; a CREF large against the stray capacitance holds it below 0.5 count.

COMMON sits about 2.8 V below V+, chosen for a battery end-of-life near 6 V. Above about 7 V total supply the internal zener regulates and COMMON has 0.001%/V voltage coefficient, about 15 Ω output impedance and under 80 ppm/°C typical. An internal N-channel FET sinks about 30 mA to hold it, but it sources only 10 µA, so COMMON is easily pulled lower to override it. COMMON is also the input-low return in auto-zero and deintegrate; where IN LO is at a fixed voltage such as supply ground, tying COMMON to the same point removes the common-mode voltage, and the reference likewise.

On the ICL7107 the LED drivers heat the die, and the plastic package's higher thermal resistance makes it worse: noise near full scale can rise from 25 µV to 80 µVp-p, linearity between a high-dissipation reading (1000, 20 segments) and a low one (1111, 8 segments) can shift a count or more, and overrange, a low-dissipation state with the lower three digits blank, can take several counts to leave with a positive-TC reference or cycle with a negative-TC one. An external reference removes all of these; the ICL7106 dissipates too little to show them.

On the ICL7106, TEST connects through 500 Ω to the internal digital supply and can be the negative rail for added segment drivers such as decimal points, loaded by 1 mA at most. On both parts, TEST pulled to V+ is a lamp test: all segments on, reading 1888, with TEST sinking about 15 mA. In lamp test the LCD segments see steady DC, which can damage the display if left on long.

The ICL7106 makes its digital ground from a 6 V zener and a large P-channel follower, stiff enough for the backplane switching currents. BP runs at the oscillator frequency divided by 800, 60 Hz at three readings a second, about 5 V in amplitude; segments switch at the same frequency, in phase with BP when off and out of phase when on, so almost no DC appears across them. The ICL7107 has no regulated supply or backplane drive and sinks 8 mA typical per segment instead of 2 mA, for common-anode LED displays; pin 19 drives two segments and sinks 16 mA. On both, the minus sign turns on for negative inputs; swapping IN HI and IN LO reverses it.

The clock is an external oscillator into OSC 1 or an RC oscillator on all three OSC pins. It is divided by four to clock the counters, then into the phases: integrate 1000 counts, deintegrate 0 to 2000 counts and auto-zero 1000 to 3000 counts, auto-zero taking whatever deintegrate leaves. A full cycle is 4000 counts (16000 oscillator periods) at any input; 48 kHz gives three readings a second. Line rejection is best when the integrate time is a whole number of line periods.

Buffer and integrator have class A outputs with 100 µA quiescent current and drive 4 µA with negligible nonlinearity. RINT is large enough to stay in that range and small enough to keep board leakage harmless: about 470 kΩ for 2 V full scale, 47 kΩ for 200 mV.

CINT gives the largest swing that tolerances cannot push into saturation, about 0.3 V from either rail. With COMMON as reference, a +2 V full-scale swing suits both parts; on an ICL7107 at ±5 V with COMMON grounded, ±3.5 V to +4 V is nominal. At 48 kHz these give 0.22 µF and 0.10 µF; at other frequencies CINT scales inversely. CINT needs low dielectric absorption to avoid rollover error; polypropylene works well.
CAZ affects noise. 0.47 µF suits the 200 mV range; on the 2 V range 0.047 µF recovers from overload faster and is quiet enough.
0.1 µF works in most cases. With a large common-mode voltage (REF LO away from COMMON) on the 200 mV range, about 1 µF keeps rollover error to 0.5 count.
Use 100 kΩ at any frequency and pick C from fOSC = 0.45/RC; 100 pF gives 48 kHz, three readings a second.

Full scale is 2 × VREF, so 100 mV for 200 mV and 1 V for 2 V. With a transducer, VREF can match its output directly: for a full-scale reading at 0.662 V, VREF = 0.341 V with 120 kΩ and 0.22 µF, avoiding an input divider and lowering noise. An ICL7107 on ±5 V accepts inputs up to ±4 V. A zero reading at a non-zero input is had by putting the transducer between IN HI and COMMON and an offset voltage between COMMON and IN LO.

The ICL7107 runs from ±5 V. Without a negative rail one can be pumped from the clock with two diodes, two capacitors and a buffer IC, or made with an ICL7660. A single +5 V supply works when the input can be referred to the middle of the common-mode range, stays within ±1.5 V, and an external reference is used.
